frequency_question: What proportion of major proposed federal agency rulemakings with high financial impact proceed to final publication within 12 months of initial substantial signal, versus those that stall or happen without standard advance notice?
membership_rule: Includes any significant or economically major federal agency notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) or interim final rule involving substantial cost changes or fee adjustments; excludes minor housekeeping rules or non-binding policy guidance.

cases.name: DHS Asylum Transit Ban Interim Final Rule (2019)
Student and Exchange Visitor Program Restrictions (2020)

coverage_note: 6 named prominent immigration and fee-related rulemaking actions; believed roughly 8 to 10 in total matching high-impact criteria during recent comparable periods.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sub-regulatory guidance documents that do not require Federal Register publication.
skeleton: Executive agency significant regulatory actions initiated via major policy signal within a presidential term, multiplied by historical completion rate within 12 months.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 6 documented high-visibility administrative rule cases
validity_reason: Base rate tied to standard administrative procedure act (APA) timelines and executive branch regulatory execution patterns, valid until the end of the current presidential administration.
